alexa (marketing): Hey @eng-runtime folks — preparing a launch claim around 3x cost reduction with our quantized routing. Can we run a quick, randomized stability probe + smokepack across quant variants so we can call out variance and tightness in the deck?

josh (eng-runtime): Yup. Can you clarify what you mean by 'randomized stability probe'? sample size, percentiles, and which models/quant packs?

alexa (marketing): Good q. Goal is a small reproducibility pack for reviewers: 200 seeds per variant, 95/99/avg latencies, token-level cost breakdown, and 5 sample outputs per seed for basic quality checks. Focus on 7B and 13B families, FP16 baseline + our 4bit/8bit quant variants.

sam (eng-runtime): That sounds reasonable. Two quick asks: 1) do you want cold-start included or only warmed hosts? 2) Are we ok with a single region (us-west-2) for this pass?

alexa (marketing): Include both: a cold-start sweep (first 50 requests after host boot) and a warmed sweep. Region: start with us-west-2 — if numbers look weird we can extend. Also please capture KV-cache hit ratio and per-request warmup time.

josh (eng-runtime): Working plan: we'll push a short runbook and smokepack. Proposed commands (will run in a dedicated QA pool):
```bash
bench-run --model redwood-13b-v1 --variant quant-4bit --seeds 0..199 --region us-west-2 --capture-traces --warmup 10 --cold-samples 50
```
We can parallelize across variants. Expect ~2h wall time.

maria (marketing-ops): Timeline check — we need artifacts (CSV latency/cost, 5 sample outputs per seed, traces) for review by EOD tomorrow. Is that feasible? :grimacing:

sam (eng-runtime): 2h run + artifact packaging + short QA => we can try to deliver within a working day if we start now. If not, we'll prioritize the 7B/13B 4bit/8bit first.

alexa (marketing): Please also: 1) randomize seed order in the pack (so reviewers can't infer ordering biases), 2) include the raw prompt set (we'll share it in this thread), and 3) tag any seeds with outlier quality or generation failures.

josh (eng-runtime): Got it. Add the prompt set to the channel and we'll ingest. We'll also emit a small metadata JSON per run with kernel selection, batch size, CUDA/cuBLAS versions, and quantization pipeline notes.

benchbot: Job 1795554321-qa-quant-run queued by josh. Estimated completion 2h. Logs will stream to https://benchstream.redwood.example/jobs/1795554321

alexa (marketing): Thanks — ping us when the CSV and sample pack are ready. If any run shows >10% latency variance at p95 vs baseline, flag so we can discuss messaging. :thumbsup:

sam (eng-runtime): Will do. If we hit unexpected variance we can add a short rerun with deterministic scheduling and a heatmap of sequence-length vs latency.

alexa (marketing): Perfect. Sending prompt set now.
